origin: From the Sanskrit avatāra, the form a god takes on descending to earth. Through the 1985 game Ultima IV and the 1992 novel Snow Crash, it came to mean the picture that stands for you online.
whenToUse: Places where people appear, such as comments, assignees, or chat partners.
People without photos still need to be told apart.
whenNotToUse: Things that aren't people (use an icon).
The name must be visible (use it with the name in text).
The photo is used to verify identity (show it larger).

alternatives.name: Presence
alternatives.reason: Also showing whether someone is online.

accessibility: Both the photo's alt and the initials' aria-label use the name.
If the photo fails to load, onError switches to initials so no broken image remains.
The initials are aria-hidden so the name isn't read twice.
The color comes from the name, so the same person always gets the same color.
